summary.summary: Oldham's 2024/25 outturn shows total borrowing up 29.6% in the year, from £181.110m to £234.817m, as the Capital Financing Requirement grew £70.859m to £559.839m. The council breached the PFI/finance-lease element of its Operational Boundary and Authorised Limit during the year (driven by an IFRS 16 recalculation of PFI lease liabilities) and is asking members to raise both limits rather than reduce the exposure. £39m of LOBO loans carried call dates within the following 12 months; a £5m LOBO with FMS Wertmanagement was called on 31 March 2025 at a proposed 7.67% rate and the council repaid it in full on 7 April 2025. Financing costs as a share of net revenue stream rose from 6.50% to 7.61% year-on-year.

signals.headline: The PFI/finance-lease element of the Operational Boundary and Authorised Limit was breached in 2024/25 (£223.812m against a £183.5m/£186.0m boundary/limit); Cabinet is asked to raise both to £230.0m/£235.0m rather than cut the exposure.
signals.why: A breached limit resolved by raising the ceiling, not reducing debt, is exactly the pattern this signal is designed to flag.

signals.headline: Total borrowing rose 29.6% in the year, from £181.110m to £234.817m (+£53.707m), almost all of it in short-term borrowing.
signals.why: A rapid rise in gross debt within a single year is worth watching for pace and refinancing implications.

signals.headline: £39m of LOBO loans had call dates within 12 months of 31 March 2025; a £5m LOBO with FMS Wertmanagement was called at 31 March 2025 (proposed rate 7.67%) and repaid in full on 7 April 2025.
signals.why: LOBO call windows can force refinancing at short notice and at rates set by the lender, not the council.

signals.headline: Financing costs as a share of net revenue stream rose from 6.50% (2023/24) to 7.61% (2024/25), as financing costs increased from £19.424m to £26.252m.
signals.why: Debt-servicing is taking a growing bite out of the revenue budget.

news_drafts.headline: Oldham faces £39m refinancing wall as costly loan calls mount
news_drafts.lead: Oldham Council faces an immediate refinancing challenge, with £39m of LOBO loans (bank borrowing where lenders can force early repayment at new rates) set to come due within the next 12 months. Two such loans were called this year at 7.67% and 6.70% respectively—240 to 340 basis points above the council's existing portfolio average of 4.33%. The looming calls represent half of Oldham's £75.5m LOBO portfolio, with counterparties including Dexia Finance and KBC Bank. Net borrowing meanwhile has risen 12.5% in one year to £210.7m, and the council is deliberately deferring external borrowing pending better market conditions while reserves are forecast to decline to £129.9m by March 2027.

findings.headline: Council maintaining under-borrowed position, deferring external borrowing while consuming reserves
findings.detail: The Council's Capital Financing Requirement stands at £369.7m but external borrowing is only £259.957m, leaving £109.7m internal borrowing (reserves and balances) deployed for capital finance. Officers are deliberately deferring new external borrowing pending 'optimum' market conditions, while the liability benchmark forecasts rapid drawdown of reserves to £129.9m by March 2027.
findings.matters: Once reserves are consumed, the council faces forced borrowing at prevailing market rates; recent LOBO calls at 6–8% demonstrate these may be substantially elevated, leaving limited financial flexibility within debt ceilings.
findings.figures: CFR £369.677m, external borrowing £259.957m, internal borrowing £109.718m, forecasted reserves March 2027 £129.936m
findings.quote: This along with raising interest rates for external debt means that the Council will continue to analyse and assess the market to determine the optimum time to externally borrow.

findings.headline: Net borrowing rose 12.5% in one year to £210.7m
findings.detail: Net borrowing increased by £23.5m from £187.2m at 31 March 2025 to £210.7m at 31 March 2026. Total borrowing rose by £25.1m to £259.957m while investments increased by only £1.4m. Financing costs increased from £26.5m to £27.0m annually, representing 7.82% of net revenue stream.
findings.matters: Rapid growth in net borrowing compresses the council's future borrowing capacity and debt service headroom, particularly concerning given £39m of LOBO loans maturing within 12 months.
findings.figures: £187.231m to £210.745m (increase of £23.514m, 12.5%), total borrowing £259.957m, financing costs £27.027m
findings.quote: On 31 March 2025, the Authority had net borrowing of £187.231m arising from its revenue and capital income and expenditure. This had risen to £210.745m by the end of 2025/26

findings.headline: £39m of LOBO loans have call dates within 12 months, creating concentrated refinancing exposure
findings.detail: At 31 March 2026, Oldham held £75.5m of LOBO loans, of which £39m have call dates within the next 12 months. Counterparties include Dexia Finance (£9m), Danske Bank, Just Retirement, and KBC Bank (£20m). This represents 50% of the LOBO portfolio and follows this year's calls at 6.70% and 7.67%.
findings.matters: Lenders controlling half the LOBO portfolio can force refinancing at rates beyond the council's control, creating uncertainty in forward debt servicing costs as demonstrated by this year's high-rate calls.
findings.figures: £75.500m total LOBO loans, £39.000m with call dates within 12 months, prior calls at 6.70–7.67%
findings.quote: As at 31st March 2026 Oldham Council has £75.500m, LOBO loans and £39.000m with call dates within the next 12 months. Of this sum, £9.000m is held with Dexia Finance over 2 loans, and the remaining £20m is 3 separate loans with three other providers, Danske Bank, Just Retirement and KBC Bank.

findings.headline: LOBO loans called at 6.70% and 7.67%, well above the 4.33% weighted average portfolio rate
findings.detail: During 2025/26, two LOBO loans were called by lenders requiring immediate refinancing. A £5m FMS Westmanagement loan was called at 7.67% and repaid 6 April 2025. A £5m Dexia loan was called at 6.70% and repaid 23 December 2025. These represent forced refinancing at rates 240–340 basis points above the council's existing LOBO portfolio average.
findings.matters: Demonstrates the council faces significant refinancing risk on structured products where lenders control the timing and cost, forcing debt servicing at rates substantially above the council's control.
findings.quote: A Call option for £5m FMS Westmanagement was called on 31st March 2025 with a proposed interest rate of 7.67% and repaid 6/4/2025. A further £5m loan to Dexia was called with a proposed interest rate of 6.70% and was also repaid 23 December 2025.

findings.headline: £2m provision for potential statutory override loss on property fund investment if rules not extended
findings.detail: The council has invested £15m in a CCLA property fund currently valued at £13.240m. The statutory override that allows councils to defer volatility charges on pooled investment funds may not be extended past 1 April 2029. The council has created a £2m specific provision to absorb potential accounting charges if the override ends and property valuations remain depressed.
findings.matters: Signals council anticipates material balance sheet charges within three years; if property values decline further or override is not extended, reserve drawdowns may be required.
findings.figures: £15m historical investment, current value £13.240m, £2m provision held
findings.quote: The Authority had set up a provision of £2.000m to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended. In view of the fact that the override may not be extended past 2029 the authority has decided to maintain this provision.
